subtopic: FlashAttention: IO-awareness, exactness, scope of speedup
learningObjective: Explain FlashAttention's core IO-aware optimization, the mechanism (tiling + online softmax + recomputation), and identify when the speedup is largest.

hardwareContext.architecture: GPU with on-chip SRAM (e.g. A100, H100)
requiredFeatures: large enough SRAM per SM to hold attention block tiles

stem: Which THREE of the following statements about FlashAttention (v1) are correct, per the paper?

options.text: FlashAttention computes attention block-by-block in on-chip SRAM using an online (numerically stable) softmax and never materializes the full N×N attention matrix in HBM; total HBM traffic drops from Θ(N²) to Θ(N²·d/M), where M is the SRAM budget.
FlashAttention produces exact attention outputs (up to floating-point ordering); it does not approximate the softmax or drop entries.

The speedup versus a naive attention kernel is largest in the memory-bound regime (long sequences where HBM traffic dominates) and can be smaller for very short sequences where the naive kernel is compute-bound on the SM.
FlashAttention's backward pass reuses the N×N attention matrix stored during the forward pass; storing this matrix is what makes the backward efficient.

explanation: A, B, C are the core claims of the FlashAttention paper. A: IO-aware tiling + online softmax. B: exact attention (no approximation). C: speedup scales with the memory-bound regime — long N is where naive attention's Θ(N²) HBM traffic dominates, so FlashAttention gains most; for very short sequences the naive kernel may already be compute-bound and FlashAttention's tiling overhead can eat into gains. D is wrong: FlashAttention deliberately does NOT store the N×N matrix; the backward recomputes intermediates from stored per-row softmax statistics.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: IO-aware tiling + online softmax + Θ(N²·d/M) HBM traffic.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: speedup is shape-dependent; largest in the memory-bound regime.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the N×N matrix is not stored; recomputation from statistics is used.

assumptions: SRAM refers to on-chip shared memory / L1 that holds a tile of Q/K/V and running statistics.
nonImplications: Does not imply the paper's specific speedup numbers (e.g. 2–4×) apply to arbitrary hardware or shapes; they are measurements on specific GPUs.
Does not imply that FlashAttention beats every attention kernel; for short N some hand-tuned baselines can match it.

performanceClaim.scope: Attention on GPU with sequence length N and head dim d; comparison against a naive unfused attention baseline
